examples/definitions/approval_gate.json: {"schema_version":1,"name":"approval-gate","description":"The ticket 15.2 human-in-the-loop demonstration: an offline `llm` draft feeds a `human_approval` gate that parks the run's branch without holding a lease or worker slot (ADR-017), and a `publish` step consumes the approved payload. Running it on the mock provider stops at `approve_publish` in `awaiting_human` while the fleet keeps executing other runs; the decision API (15.3) resumes it. `publish` reads `${{ steps.approve_publish.output.payload }}` — the approved value, which the decision (15.3) makes the step's output — so the gate is transparent to the rest of the graph.","params":{"topic":{"type":"string","required":true}},"steps":[{"id":"draft","type":"llm","config":{"model":"mock/sim-1","prompt":"Draft an article about ${{ run.params.topic }}.","max_tokens":128}},{"id":"approve_publish","type":"human_approval","config":{"title":"Publish this article?","description":"Review the draft before it goes live.","payload":"${{ steps.draft.output }}","allowed_decisions":["approve","reject"],"allow_edit":true,"edit_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"text":{"type":"string"}}},"timeout":"48h","on_timeout":"reject","on_reject":"fail"}},{"id":"publish","type":"echo","config":{"input":{"published":"${{ steps.approve_publish.output.payload }}"}}}],"edges":[{"from":"draft","to":"approve_publish"},{"from":"approve_publish","to":"publish"}]}
examples/definitions/approval_reject_rou: {"schema_version":1,"name":"approval-reject-route","description":"The ticket 15.3 reject-routing demonstration: a `human_approval` gate with `on_reject: route`. A rejected decision does not fail the run — the gate *succeeds* with `decision: reject` and fires only its `decision: reject` edge (to `notify_rejected`), while the unmarked approve edge (to `publish`) is skipped by ordinary skip propagation (ADR-017). An approve decision fires the approve edge and skips the reject edge instead. Either way the run completes; the author's choice of a dedicated reject branch versus a fail branch (`on_reject: fail`, the default in approval_gate.json) is a graph-shape decision the `decision` edge marker makes explicit and UI-renderable.","params":{"topic":{"type":"string","required":true}},"steps":[{"id":"draft","type":"llm","config":{"model":"mock/sim-1","prompt":"Draft an article about ${{ run.params.topic }}.","max_tokens":128}},{"id":"review","type":"human_approval","config":{"title":"Publish or send back?","description":"Approve to publish, reject to route the draft back for revision.","payload":"${{ steps.draft.output }}","allowed_decisions":["approve","reject"],"on_reject":"route"}},{"id":"publish","type":"echo","config":{"input":{"published":"${{ steps.review.output.payload }}"}}},{"id":"notify_rejected","type":"echo","config":{"input":{"rejected":true,"comment":"${{ steps.review.output.comment }}"}}}],"edges":[{"from":"draft","to":"review"},{"from":"review","to":"publish"},{"from":"review","to":"notify_rejected","decision":"reject"}]}
examples/definitions/approval_timeout_ap: {"schema_version":1,"name":"approval-timeout-approve","description":"The ticket 15.4 auto-approve-on-timeout demonstration: a `human_approval` gate whose `on_timeout` policy is `approve` (documented as dangerous — a side effect fires with no human in the loop; only for gates where \"no answer means go\"). On park the executor schedules an expiry through the delayed queue due at `timeout_at`; when it fires, the timeout policy auto-approves the ORIGINAL payload (never an edit) through the same single-arbiter CAS a human decision uses, records the approval `expired` with `decision: approve` / `source: timeout` / `decided_by: system:timeout`, and `publish` consumes the approved payload. A human decision arriving first wins the CAS and best-effort cancels the pending expiry.","params":{"topic":{"type":"string","required":true}},"steps":[{"id":"draft","type":"llm","config":{"model":"mock/sim-1","prompt":"Draft an article about ${{ run.params.topic }}.","max_tokens":128}},{"id":"approve_publish","type":"human_approval","config":{"title":"Publish this article?","description":"Review the draft before it goes live; no answer means go.","payload":"${{ steps.draft.output }}","allowed_decisions":["approve","reject"],"timeout":"24h","on_timeout":"approve"}},{"id":"publish","type":"echo","config":{"input":{"published":"${{ steps.approve_publish.output.payload }}"}}}],"edges":[{"from":"draft","to":"approve_publish"},{"from":"approve_publish","to":"publish"}]}
examples/definitions/approval_timeout_pa: {"schema_version":1,"name":"approval-timeout-park","description":"The ticket 15.4 escalate-on-timeout demonstration: a `human_approval` gate whose `on_timeout` policy is `park`. When the expiry fires, the approval stays `pending` (still decidable) and the RUN parks with the reserved `park_reason = awaiting_human` as an escalation — no decision is recorded, the side effect never fires unattended. The park is idempotent (a stamped `expired_at` marks the run was parked once, so a redelivered or reconciler-healed expiry never re-parks). A later human decision resolves the gate through the ordinary park-tolerant decision path, and `unpark` resumes the run's other work — so \"timeout policy park leaves the run resumable via unpark\" holds.","params":{"topic":{"type":"string","required":true}},"steps":[{"id":"draft","type":"llm","config":{"model":"mock/sim-1","prompt":"Draft an article about ${{ run.params.topic }}.","max_tokens":128}},{"id":"approve_publish","type":"human_approval","config":{"title":"Publish this article?","description":"Review the draft before it goes live; no answer escalates.","payload":"${{ steps.draft.output }}","allowed_decisions":["approve","reject"],"timeout":"24h","on_timeout":"park","on_reject":"fail"}},{"id":"publish","type":"echo","config":{"input":{"published":"${{ steps.approve_publish.output.payload }}"}}}],"edges":[{"from":"draft","to":"approve_publish"},{"from":"approve_publish","to":"publish"}]}
examples/definitions/blackboard.json: {"schema_version":1,"name":"blackboard","description":"The ticket 12.2 (ADR-014) demonstration of the run-scoped blackboard: shared, versioned key/value memory steps read and write during a run. A draft `llm` step (offline mock, model `mock/sim-1`) publishes its completion text to the blackboard declaratively via its `blackboard` block — pinned so no future compaction (M12.4) can drop it — while its `from: /text` pointer selects exactly the completion text. In parallel a `blackboard_write` step records a plan under key `plan` with a `writer` tag. A join gathers both, then a `capstone` `blackboard_write` writes key `plan` again under a version compare-and-swap guard (`expected_version: 1`, so it lands at v2 only if nothing else moved the key) and reads the pinned `draft_text` head back through `read_key`. Every entry is token-counted with the writing step's counter (the llm step's model tokenizer, the chars/4 fallback for the plain writes) and retained for audit. Runs entirely offline on the mock provider — no API key, no network — so it is the workhorse blackboard fixture for CI. Inspect the result with `ctl blackboard <run-id>` or GET /v1/runs/{id}/blackboard.","steps":[{"id":"start","type":"noop"},{"id":"draft","type":"llm","config":{"model":"mock/sim-1","prompt":"Draft an opening paragraph.","max_tokens":128},"blackboard":{"write":[{"key":"draft_text","from":"/text","tags":["draft"],"pinned":true}]}},{"id":"plan","type":"blackboard_write","config":{"key":"plan","value":{"steps":["research","write","review"]},"tags":["writer"]}},{"id":"gather","type":"join","config":{"mode":"all"}},{"id":"capstone","type":"blackboard_write","config":{"key":"plan","value":{"steps":["research","write","review","publish"],"revised":true},"expected_version":1,"read_key":"draft_text"}}],"edges":[{"from":"start","to":"draft"},{"from":"start","to":"plan"},{"from":"draft","to":"gather"},{"from":"plan","to":"gather"},{"from":"gather","to":"capstone"}]}

examples/definitions/context_assembly.js: {"schema_version":1,"name":"context_assembly","description":"The ticket 12.3 (ADR-014) demonstration of declarative context assembly: a step declares an ordered `context` spec whose sources — upstream step outputs, blackboard entries by key or tag, retrieval results, and inline literals — are assembled into the provider request before the call, with per-source token caps and pinned entries always included, deterministic given store state. A `research` `llm` step (offline mock, model `mock/sim-1`) publishes its completion text to the blackboard under key `findings` (tag `research`) via its `blackboard` write block. The `draft` `llm` step then assembles four sources in precedence order: a pinned `literal` of editor instructions (never dropped or truncated by future compaction, M12.4); the `research` step's `/text` output capped at 2000 tokens; the pinned `findings` blackboard head by key; and a `pg_fulltext` retrieval of a style guide with `on_missing: skip` so an empty corpus omits it with an audit event rather than failing the step. Assembly prepends the rendered context to the prompt, re-keying the response cache and the pre-flight token total by construction; the total is recorded on the `context_assembled` event alongside each source's included/skipped/truncated disposition. Runs entirely offline on the mock provider — no API key, no network — so it is the workhorse context-assembly fixture for CI. Inspect the blackboard with `ctl blackboard <run-id>`; the assembly manifest is on the run's event log.","steps":[{"id":"research","type":"llm","config":{"model":"mock/sim-1","prompt":"Research the topic and list the key findings.","max_tokens":256},"blackboard":{"write":[{"key":"findings","from":"/text","tags":["research"],"pinned":true}]}},{"id":"draft","type":"llm","config":{"model":"mock/sim-1","prompt":"Write a first draft grounded in the research and style guide above.","max_tokens":512},"context":{"sources":[{"kind":"literal","name":"instructions","text":"You are a careful writer. {"schema_version":1,"name":"context_compaction","description":"The ticket 12.4 (ADR-014) demonstration of deterministic context compaction: a five-turn conversation (offline mock, model mock/sim-1) each writes its turn to the run blackboard under key turn_N (tag `turn`), and a final `summary` `llm` step assembles a pinned scribe instruction plus all five turns by key into its request. The assembled context exceeds the step's tight `budget_tokens` (200), so the ordered compaction pipeline runs: `sliding_window` (n=3) keeps only the three most-recent turns and drops turn_1/turn_2; `truncate_oldest` (min_tokens=32) middle-out-truncates the oldest survivor with an elision marker if still over; `drop_lowest_priority` evicts the lowest-priority remaining turn as a last resort. The pinned instruction is never dropped or truncated. Each strategy that runs writes a `context_revision` event (tokens before/after, entries dropped/kept), and the final request is guaranteed at or under budget before the provider is ever called — a context-overflow 400 is structurally impossible. Runs entirely offline on the mock provider (no API key, no network), so it is the workhorse compaction fixture for CI. Inspect the run event log for the `context_revision` and `context_assembled` records; the surviving turns are on the blackboard via `ctl blackboard examples/definitions/context_summarizati: {"schema_version":1,"name":"context_summarization","description":"The ticket 12.5 (ADR-014) demonstration of summarization compaction: a sixteen-turn conversation (offline mock, model mock/sim-1) writes each turn to the run blackboard under key turn_N (tag `turn`). The assembly exceeds the budget, so the ordered compaction pipeline runs: the `summarize` strategy folds the oldest evicted turns with a cheap model (mock/cheap, temperature 0) into a summary written to the blackboard under key `context_summary`, chaining a new version each rollup (parent_version links the chain); `drop_lowest_priority` is the deterministic fallback if the summarizer is unavailable. Runs entirely offline on the mock provider (no API key, no network). examples/definitions/context_window.json: {"schema_version":1,"name":"context_window","description":"The ticket 12.6 (ADR-014) demonstration of provider-window guardrails: the same five-turn conversation as context_compaction.json, but on the small-window model `mock/small` (context_window 1024 tokens in the pricing catalog) and with NO explicit `budget_tokens`. The final `summary` step reserves a large completion (`max_tokens` 700), so the window-derived default budget — window − max_tokens − 5% headroom — is tight, and the assembled pinned-instruction-plus-five-turns context exceeds it. The engine defaults the budget from the model context window (`budget_source: window` on the context_assembled event) and runs the ordered compaction pipeline (sliding_window → truncate_oldest → drop_lowest_priority) until the framed request fits, so `assembled + max_tokens <= context_window` holds and a provider context-overflow 400 is structurally impossible — with zero per-workflow budget authoring. Runs entirely offline on the mock provider (no API key, no network). Inspect the run event log for the `context_assembled` (carrying `budget_source`, `budget_tokens`, `context_window`) and `context_revision` records.","steps":[{"id":"turn1","type":"llm","config":{"model":"mock/small","prompt":"Turn one: we kicked off the project and agreed the north-star metric is weekly active teams, not raw signups, examples/definitions/echo_pipeline.json: {"schema_version":1,"name":"echo-pipeline","description":"The ticket 8.2 data-flow proof: a three-step echo chain where every value moves between steps through `${{ ... }}` template expressions — run params into the first step (including a whole-object param preserved as JSON), nested-path references and string interpolation in the second, and a multi-hop third step that reaches two hops upstream, passes a whole output object through by reference, and exercises the full restricted function set (get with a lenient path, default, toJson, truncate). Echo steps output exactly their rendered input, so each step's recorded output is a direct probe of what rendering resolved.","params":{"audience":{"type":"object","required":true},"greeting":{"type":"string","required":true}},"steps":[{"id":"compose","type":"echo","config":{"input":{"text":"${{ run.params.greeting }}","audience":"${{ run.params.audience }}"}}},{"id":"headline","type":"echo","config":{"input":"${{ steps.compose.output.text }}, ${{ steps.compose.output.audience.name }}!"}},{"id":"package","type":"echo","config":{"input":{"headline":"${{ steps.headline.output }}","teaser":"${{ steps.headline.output | truncate 10 }}","bundle":"${{ steps.compose.output }}","audience_json":"${{ steps.compose.output.audience | toJson }}","signoff":"${{ get 'steps.compose.output.audience.signoff' | default 'kind regards' }}"}}}],"edges":[{"from":"compose","to":"headline"},{"from":"headline","to":"package"}]}
examples/definitions/fanout.json: {"schema_version":1,"name":"fanout-fanin","description":"Parallel fan-out and fan-in: one entry step fans out to three independent research steps (multiple unconditioned out-edges run in parallel), which converge on a `join all` barrier before a final synthesis step. Demonstrates parallel execution and all-parents join semantics.","params":{"topic":{"type":"string","required":true}},"steps":[{"id":"start","type":"noop"},{"id":"search_docs","type":"retrieve","config":{"retriever":"pg_fulltext","query":"${{ run.params.topic }}","top_k":8}},{"id":"fetch_news","type":"tool","config":{"tool":"json_transform","input":{"expr":"{ query: .topic, source: \"news\" }","input":{"topic":"${{ run.params.topic }}"}}}},{"id":"brainstorm","type":"llm","config":{"model":"mock/sim-1","prompt":"List five distinct angles for covering this topic: ${{ run.params.topic }}","max_tokens":512}},{"id":"gather","type":"join","config":{"mode":"all"}},{"id":"synthesize","type":"llm","config":{"model":"mock/sim-1","prompt":"Combine the retrieved documents, news results, and brainstormed angles into a single research brief on ${{ run.params.topic }}.","max_tokens":1024}}],"edges":[{"from":"start","to":"search_docs"},{"from":"start","to":"fetch_news"},{"from":"start","to":"brainstorm"},{"from":"search_docs","to":"gather"},{"from":"fetch_news","to":"gather"},{"from":"brainstorm","to":"gather"},{"from":"gather","to":"synthesize"}]}
examples/definitions/linear.json: {"schema_version":1,"name":"linear-pipeline","description":"The simplest possible workflow: a straight three-step chain with no conditions — fetch a page (tool), summarize it (llm), record the result (echo). Demonstrates sequential dependency edges, a required run parameter referenced from step config, and an explicit retry policy on the network-bound step (ADR-006; the other steps inherit engine defaults).","params":{"url":{"type":"string","required":true}},"steps":[{"id":"fetch","type":"tool","config":{"tool":"http_request","input":{"method":"GET","url":"${{ run.params.url }}"}},"retry":{"max_attempts":3,"backoff":{"initial":"1s","cap":"30s"}}},{"id":"summarize","type":"llm","config":{"model":"anthropic/claude-sonnet-5","prompt":"Summarize the following page in three bullet points:\n\n${{ steps.fetch.output.body }}","max_tokens":512}},{"id":"store","type":"echo","config":{"input":{"summary":"${{ steps.summarize.output.text }}"}}}],"edges":[{"from":"fetch","to":"summarize"},{"from":"summarize","to":"store"}]}
examples/definitions/map_fanout.json: {"schema_version":1,"name":"map-fanout","description":"The ticket 13.4 canonical dynamic map fan-out workflow (ADR-015). A `map` step fans a runtime list out into one instance of a named sub-template (the `templates` library) per item, plus a generated `gather` join that collects the ordered per-instance results — an engine-generated expansion (no LLM), applied atomically through store.ExpandRun exactly like a planner's. Here `source` emits a three-element list, `process` maps over it (instantiating `analyze_one` as `analyze#0..2`, each an `llm` call on `mock/sim-1` that references its item through the reserved `${{ item }}` / `${{ item_index }}` roots), and the generated gather `process#gather` emits the ordered array of the three analyses. It runs entirely offline on the mock: the mock echoes each prompt, so the gathered array cites each item verbatim. N is capped by `max_items` (and by the run's per-expansion cap); a list longer than the cap fails the map permanently at expansion time. Swap `source` for a `retrieve` and `mock/sim-1` for a real provider and the same shape maps an LLM call over a retrieved list.","templates":{"analyze_one":{"steps":[{"id":"analyze","type":"llm","config":{"model":"mock/sim-1","prompt":"Analyze item ${{ item_index }}: ${{ item }}","max_tokens":64,"temperature":0}}]}},"steps":[{"id":"source","type":"echo","config":{"input":{"items":["alpha","beta","gamma"]}}},{"id":"process","type":"map","config":{"items":"${{ steps.source.output.items }}","body":"analyze_one","max_items":100}}],"edges":[{"from":"source","to":"process"}]}
examples/definitions/mock_pipeline.json: {"schema_version":1,"name":"mock-pipeline","description":"The ticket 8.5 proof that two chained `llm` steps pass data between them through templating, running entirely on the deterministic offline mock provider (model `mock/sim-1`). A converted linear M4 chain: a draft step turns a run param into a completion, a refine step feeds that completion back into a second model call via `${{ steps.draft.output.text }}`, and a record step captures the final text. On the mock the outputs are reproducible with no API key and no network, so this is the workhorse fixture for CI and load; swapping the model id to a real provider makes it a live workflow unchanged.","params":{"topic":{"type":"string","required":true}},"steps":[{"id":"draft","type":"llm","config":{"model":"mock/sim-1","prompt":"Draft a note about ${{ run.params.topic }}.","max_tokens":128}},{"id":"refine","type":"llm","config":{"model":"mock/sim-1","prompt":"Improve this draft: ${{ steps.draft.output.text }}","max_tokens":128}},{"id":"record","type":"echo","config":{"input":{"final":"${{ steps.refine.output.text }}"}}}],"edges":[{"from":"draft","to":"refine"},{"from":"refine","to":"record"}]}
examples/definitions/planner.json: {"schema_version":1,"name":"planner-expansion","description":"The ticket 13.3 canonical dynamic-DAG workflow (ADR-015). A `planner` step is an `llm` call whose validated output — a PlanOutput document — is spliced into the running graph atomically with the planner's completion (store.ExpandRun): the plan injects two `llm` worker steps that depend on the planner (an `after` splice, `plan -> work_*`) and fan into a pre-existing `gather` join (a `before` splice, `work_* -> gather`, widening the join's dependency count). The injected steps then execute like any authored step, the join continues once both land, and the run succeeds. The plan is gated by an implicit json_schema validator over the published plan-output.v1.json schema (a malformed plan would route to the semantic-retry loop, repaired with the rejection issues as feedback, `max_attempts` 3) and by the run's expansion caps. It runs entirely offline on the mock (model `mock/sim-1`): the planner's prompt IS a valid PlanOutput, which the mock's structured-echo returns verbatim — swap the prompt for a real instruction and the model id for a real provider and the planner generates the plan itself, unchanged.","expansion":{"max_added_steps":16,"max_expansions":10,"max_depth":2},"steps":[{"id":"plan","type":"planner","config":{"model":"mock/sim-1","prompt":"{\"schema_version\":1,\"steps\":[{\"id\":\"work_a\",\"type\":\"llm\",\"config\":{\"model\":\"mock/sim-1\",\"prompt\":\"Analyze part A\",\"max_tokens\":64,\"temperature\":0}},{\"id\":\"work_b\",\"type\":\"llm\",\"config\":{\"model\":\"mock/sim-1\",\"prompt\":\"Analyze part B\",\"max_tokens\":64,\"temperature\":0}}],\"edges\":[{\"from\":\"plan\",\"to\":\"work_a\"},{\"from\":\"plan\",\"to\":\"work_b\"},{\"from\":\"work_a\",\"to\":\"gather\"},{\"from\":\"work_b\",\"to\":\"gather\"}]}","max_tokens":512,"temperature":0,"max_added_steps":8},"validation":{"max_attempts":3}},{"id":"gather","type":"join","config":{"mode":"all"}},{"id":"report","type":"echo","config":{"input":{"status":"plan executed and gathered"}}}],"edges":[{"from":"plan","to":"gather"},{"from":"gather","to":"report"}]}
examples/definitions/rag_lite.json: {"schema_version":1,"name":"rag-lite","description":"The ticket 8.8 retrieval-augmented-generation proof: a `retrieve` step queries the reference `pg_fulltext` retriever for the documents most relevant to a run param, then an `llm` step answers the question grounded in those documents and cites each by id. Data flows from retrieve to llm through 8.2 templating — `${{ steps.search.output.results }}` splices the ranked results (an array of {id, content, score, metadata}) into the prompt as compact JSON. It runs fully offline: the retriever is local Postgres full-text search over an ingested corpus, and the model is the deterministic mock (`mock/sim-1`), so the answer is reproducible with no API key and no network; swapping the model id to a real provider makes it a live RAG workflow unchanged.","params":{"question":{"type":"string","required":true}},"steps":[{"id":"search","type":"retrieve","config":{"retriever":"pg_fulltext","query":"${{ run.params.question }}","top_k":3}},{"id":"answer","type":"llm","config":{"model":"mock/sim-1","prompt":"Answer the question \"${{ run.params.question }}\" using only the retrieved documents below, and cite each claim with the document id it came from. Documents: ${{ steps.search.output.results }}","max_tokens":512}}],"edges":[{"from":"search","to":"answer"}]}
{"schema_version":1,"name":"structured-extract","description":"The ticket 11.3 canonical structured-output workflow (ADR-013). An `llm` extract step declares an `output_format` with a JSON Schema: the engine asks the mock provider for native structured output, deterministically JSON-repairs the completion when it arrives as text instead, and runs an implicit `json_schema` validator over the result — so an output that cannot be shaped into schema-conforming JSON dead-letters as validation_failed rather than flowing on malformed. The structured `.json` then flows into a downstream `record` step through `${{ steps.extract.output.json.echo }}`. It runs entirely offline on the mock (model `mock/sim-1`), whose native structured answer is a JSON object `{\"echo\": <text>}` matching the schema; swapping the model id and schema for a real provider makes it a live extraction workflow unchanged.","params":{"document":{"type":"string","required":true}},"steps":[{"id":"extract","type":"llm","config":{"model":"mock/sim-1","prompt":"Extract the salient text from this document as JSON: ${{ run.params.document }}","max_tokens":256,"temperature":0,"output_format":{"type":"json_schema","schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"echo":{"type":"string"}},"required":["echo"],"additionalProperties":true},"mode":"auto"}}},{"id":"record","type":"echo","config":{"input":{"extracted":"${{ steps.extract.output.json.echo }}"}}}],"edges":[{"from":"extract","to":"record"}]}
